citations.claim: NS still green just before transition, showing excessively long green phase
NS yellow still active on last yellow second (4th second)
First violating step: NS already red/all-red, yellow lasted only 4s vs required 6s

counterfactual.change: actuated true -> false (fixed-time). Same green/yellow/all_red and arrivals and steps. Isolates actuated controller as cause: fixed-time respects yellow_seconds and no violation.

explanation: Shrunk actuated scenario holds NS green for ~151 s (steps 0-150, see step 150 NS green) far beyond max_green_seconds 90, then truncates the following NS yellow to 4 s instead of required 6 s. Inspect shows NS yellow starts at 151 and ends at 154 (only steps 151-154 =4 s) with phase all-red before EW at 155, violating yellow_seconds 6. The actuated gap-out / max-green logic likely does not enforce max_green and then cuts yellow short to service the long-waiting EW direction (EW wait 87-91s at 150-154). Fixed-time with same timings respects the 6s yellow, proving actuated timing is the cause.
vision_note: Steps 152-154 show the NS approaches on yellow (yellow dots) while EW is red. By step 155 all four approaches are red, so the yellow was only ~4 seconds long before the all-red clearance, truncating the required 6s yellow.
